fundamental theorem of calculus.d: Adding up a rate gives the total change: ∫₀¹ q′(s) ds = q(1) − q(0). Example: integrating a car's speed over a trip gives the distance travelled, which is what an odometer does.

threshold site.d: A one-input nonlinear node (SiLU, sigmoid, exp, …) seen as a source of curvature. It adds ḡ·θ″(z)·a aᵀ: rank 1, one-signed, along its read a (theory-v2 Lemma 2).

product site.d: A node that multiplies two quantities, seen as a source of curvature. It adds ḡ·(a bᵀ + b aᵀ): one up-curving and one down-curving direction (inertia (1,1)). A SwiGLU neuron, silu(gate read) × up read, is one.

Gauss–Newton term.d: In the Hessian of a loss of a network's output, the part Jᵀ(∇²loss)J: the loss's own curvature carried through the network's Jacobian. It is never negative along any direction when the loss is convex.

explained variance.d: How much of the spread of the true values a predictor accounts for: 1 minus (sum of squared misses) ÷ (sum of squared deviations from the mean). 1 is perfect; below 0 means worse than always guessing the average.

relative L1 error.d: Sum of absolute prediction misses divided by the sum of absolute true values. 0 is perfect; 1 means the misses are as large as the values themselves.
